source_text.body:
Use an AI assistant for news, recipes, workouts and email
The author uses an AI app in place of websites for sourced news, recipes, exercise routines and email management, and has Claude build artifacts to render data.
·
Nov 18, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
The author uses an AI app instead of visiting websites for news, recipes, exercise routines and email management. For news, the assistant searches the web and returns answers with cited sources. When they want information laid out more readably, they ask Claude to build an artifact that renders the data as a simple website.
How it went
The author says the experience beats ad-heavy, paywalled sites, and one small monthly subscription covers it all with no ads. The comment gives no figures or failure cases.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
For the next week, act as my replacement for news sites, recipe sites and workout apps. Each morning give me a short news roundup on [topics] with sources linked, suggest a dinner recipe using [ingredients or dietary needs], and propose a [length]-minute workout for [goal and equipment]. When I give you data such as a weekly workout log or a meal plan, build an artifact that displays it clearly. Before you send, delete or archive anything in my email, show me exactly what you plan to do and wait for my approval.
Original source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50543661
